newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU labour, employers to discuss plant closures.
newsitem.headline: EU labour, employers to discuss plant closures.

text.p: Representatives of European employer and trade union groups agreed on Tuesday to open talks aimed at drawing up guidelines for consulting workers when companies decide to shut down operations.

Dutch Employment Minister Ad Melkert, who called the meeting in the wake of the much-criticised decision by French carmaker Renault to close its Vilvoorde plant in Belgium, said the two sides would try to agree how to interpret European Union rules on the question.
Melkert, whose country holds the EU presidency, told a news conference they would work to clarify, for example, how much notice companies should give workers about restructuring plans.

The meeting was attended by Zygmunt Tyszkiewicz, secretary general of the European employers group UNICE, Emilio Gabaglio, secretary general of the European Trade Union Confederation, and EU Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn.
In a statement, Melkert and Flynn said worker consultation was effective only if it was "carried out well in advance".
The EU's European Works Council directive, 94/45/EC, requires multinational companies to consult workers about major reorganisations "as soon as possible" after the decision has been made.
French and Belgian courts ruled that Renault had violated EU law and could not close its Vilvoorde plant until it had consulted the workers.
Melkert said a code of conduct would be a quicker way to address the problem than the EU's time-consuming legislative process.

But Flynn said the European Commission was studying whether EU legislation should be strengthened to apply sanctions to companies that violate EU rules -- for example, declaring dismissals "null and void" if workers were not properly informed.

He said that question and the issue of "timeliness" of consultations would be addressed in talks that will be opened soon between labour and employer groups on new EU rules to govern worker consultation at companies operating only at national level.
Melkert organised Tuesday's meeting in response to a call by EU social affairs ministers in March at an informal meeting in Rotterdam for a clear code of conduct governing business closures.

He said he had asked UNICE and ETUC to try to make progress in their talks before EU social affairs ministers meet in June. He said the public-sector employers group CEEP would also participate in the talks.
